description: For team-related communication, collaboration, and updates regarding NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, please contact our team leader through the provided email address or WhatsApp. We welcome communication from team members regarding project discussions, task coordination, meetings, and important announcements. Our team is committed to maintaining clear communication and effective collaboration throughout the challenge.
summary: Paati’s Stories Beyond the Stars is an interactive, continuous-scroll children’s storybook built for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge that brings Apollo 11 and Lunar Module Eagle (LM-5) to young learners through warmth, culture, and real historical science. Inspired by SBS “The Boat” storytelling, a Southern Indian grandmother (Paati) and her curious grandson (Kanna) journey from their twilight village verandah to Tranquility Base across 36 WebGL parallax story scenes, bilingual-warm neural character narration, an interactive two-stage Eagle LM-5 explorer, an authentic 1969 NASA photo scrapbook, and Paati’s Space Notebook. Instead of dense adult tables, children learn real NASA timelines, the distinction between Saturn V, Columbia, and Eagle, lunar science experiments, and how Apollo 11 launched safely—sparking wonder grounded directly in verified NASA historical archives.
details:
What It Does and How It Works:

Paati's Stories Beyond the Stars tells the true 1969 story of Apollo 11 through the comforting evening conversation of grandmother Paati and grandson Kanna. As readers scroll smoothly (or use Auto Scroll), a custom WebGL stage cross-fades across 45 illustrated story scenes synchronized to 45 South Indian English neural character voice lines and procedural Web Audio Moonlit Music-Box bedtime background music with automatic voice ducking. Afterward, children tap parts of an interactive two-stage Lunar Module Eagle diagram, browse 5 unmodified 1969 NASA photographs, and open Paati's Space Notebook on the About page to verify every mission clock and source.

Intended Impact and Creativity:

Designed specifically for children so real space history feels warm and memorable rather than overwhelming, blending cultural storytelling with accurate Apollo 11 engineering facts (separating the roles of Apollo 11, Saturn V, Columbia, and Eagle, and distinguishing the 21h 36m lunar stay from the 2h 31m outdoor moonwalk).

Tools and Tech Stack:

React 18, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Framer Motion, React Router, Lucide Icons, custom WebGL shaders, and Web Audio API.

Super Intelligence (SI) Disclosure:

Images and Diagrams: All 21 generated storybook scene and character illustrations carry visible SI-Generated or SI-Gen watermark pills and exclude all NASA logos, flags, and mission identifiers. The 5 authentic 1969 NASA archive photographs remain unwatermarked with credits.

Audio: All 45 spoken narration clips were generated with Microsoft Edge Neural TTS and 48 kHz audio processing, with SI disclosure embedded in each audio file's container metadata and manifest. Gentle Moonlit Music-Box bedtime music is synthesized live in the browser via Web Audio API.

Code and Data: Application code, kid-friendly dialogue, and mission summaries were created with SI assistance and verified against official NASA Apollo 11 publications, with disclosures in app metadata and the About page. Independent educational project; not endorsed by NASA.
